- High: The covenant EBITDA definition and the reported first lien net leverage ratio are not printed; only a compliance statement is given. Covenant headroom is therefore not established, and no covenant conclusion should rest on the consolidated leverage ratios computed here. The executed Credit Agreement and the compliance certificate would close this. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113 - Medium: Last-twelve-months EBITDA to 2026-09-30 includes EFC from 2026-01-02 and Micromax from 2026-02-02 only, while debt is counted in full, so leverage at 2026-09-30 is overstated against run-rate. Pro forma acquired EBITDA for the full period is not stated; the issuer states only a nine-month figure assuming the Micromax acquisition closed on 2026-01-01 and a 2026 guidance figure. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 4 - Medium: The term loan principal is not scheduled by year at 2026-09-30, and USD 12.9 million of current installments beyond the USD 15.0 million revolver borrowings is not itemised. The maturity ladder places the term loans at 2030-12-18, so earlier amortisation is not shown. The Credit Agreement amortisation schedule would close this. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 8 - Medium: The filings print a dash for several lines in some periods, and each dash is treated as not supplied rather than zero: current installments of long-term debt at 2025-12-31, income from discontinued operations in FY2025, acquisition spend in FY2025 and nine months 2025, debt proceeds in FY2025 and nine months 2025, share repurchases in FY2024, financing fees in FY2025 and nine months 2025, disposal and divestiture proceeds in FY2024 and nine months 2026, non-controlling interest in the third quarters, and the add-backs for the inventory step-up, the divestiture result, debt financing costs and contingent consideration in the periods where they did not arise. The lines affected are visible in the statement tables and none is needed for a ratio; confirmation from the issuer would close them. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 82–85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7 - Low: Some statement lines exist in only one type of filing: net income from continuing operations, discontinued operations and held-for-sale lines appear in the annual statements only, and the contingent consideration line, lines of credit and the financing fee line appear in the quarterly statements only. The interim columns show those lines as not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 82–85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7 - Low: The undrawn revolver at 2024-12-31 is not stated; the annual report gives unused capacity of USD 368 million at 2025-12-31 and combined availability of about USD 390 million across all facilities at both year-ends. The liquidity table shows the 2024 figure as not supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114 - Low: Quarterly lease liabilities are not printed in the third-quarter report, so the lease obligation at 2026-09-30 is not supplied; the annual report gives USD 86.0 million at 2025-12-31 against USD 81.6 million a year earlier. Lease liabilities sit in accrued and other liabilities and are not in Total Debt. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7 - Low: The 10-Q prints no cash interest or tax supplement, so nine-month cash interest paid comes from the third-quarter release; a Q4 2025 stand-alone period and the 2025 quarterly filings are not supplied, so any quarterly trend before 2026 is not available. facts.text: The view would move to high risk if capital returns were debt-funded while leverage stayed elevated, for instance buybacks continuing at the third-quarter pace of USD 37.7 million a quarter while revolver borrowings rise, or if a further large combination were announced before the 2026 acquisitions are absorbed. It would move to low risk if the proxy statement showed independent board control and no related-party leakage beyond the advisory fee, and if the credit agreement showed restricted-payment capacity that is tight relative to current leverage. Evidence that electronics demand is slowing, such as falling organic growth in the Electronics segment from 18% in nine months 2026, would raise business risk independently of governance. facts.label: Porter's Five Forces
facts.text: Rivalry is moderate: named competitors include larger groups, but competition is on qualification, technology and service, which favours incumbents with embedded products. New entrants face qualification and technical-service barriers, which protects margin; substitutes arise through technology change such as chromium-free plating, which the company addresses with research and development. Buyer power is limited by diversification, as no customer reaches 10% of net sales, but large electronics manufacturers can resist price outside qualified products; supplier power is low for most raw materials, which are obtainable from multiple sources, with metals priced through to customers. facts.text: A slowdown in AI-linked electronics demand would reach revenue within quarters because backlog is minimal, and Electronics produces 76.2% of segment Adjusted EBITDA; operating leverage on a cost base that includes research, technical service and integration cost would compress margin, while a fall in metal prices would release working capital and cushion cash flow. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Element Solutions presents an adequate business profile supported by consumable recurring demand, customer diversification and strong interest cover, but credit quality is constrained by higher leverage after debt-funded acquisitions and concentration in Electronics. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to modest capital intensity and a fixed-rate cost of debt, with 2026 working-capital drag expected to be partly timing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of acquired earnings, early action on the 2028 notes and the rate environment when swaps expire. The primary downside path is an electronics demand slowdown while leverage is elevated and capital returns continue. Further analysis would require covenant definitions, ratings and market pricing, and acquired earnings. Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top risk: leverage after debt-funded acquisitions. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05; calculation C08

Scope is whether the seven supplied filings and releases support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit, and which other modules the sources can or cannot support.

No analysis from another module was supplied to this module.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit through 2026-09-30, but leave covenant, priority, recovery and pricing conclusions unsupported because no executed credit agreement, indenture, rating or market quote was supplied.

Creditors should read 2026 as an acquisition year: two acquisitions closed in January and February 2026, and the proposed merger with Solstice was announced in July and terminated on 2026-08-27, so the third-quarter filings control wherever earlier ones differ. Governance and ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the two acquisition prices differ between filings. Each difference is logged as a conflict rather than reconciled.

## Gaps

- Material: Neither the executed credit agreement and its amendments nor the indenture for the 2028 senior notes was supplied, and the run settings declare no legal documents. The filings summarise the facilities, the security package and one springing first lien net leverage test, so Legal & covenants cannot be assessed and any covenant, priority or recovery conclusion would rest on summaries only. Supplying the executed agreements would close this.

- Material: The annual report incorporates board, independence, executive pay and ownership detail by reference to the 2026 proxy statement, which was not supplied. Business & governance can state only what the annual report, the quarterly related-party note and the signature pages show. Obtaining the proxy statement would close this.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-07-27_aearningsreleaseex99120266.htm.jsonl, page 8

- Material: Two acquisitions closed in 2026, on 2026-01-02 and 2026-02-02, so 2026 periods are not like-for-like with 2025 and the 2025 balance sheet excludes both. The issuer's organic growth figures and its pro forma note are issuer measures, not a restated 2025 base; Financial foundation must keep reported, organic and acquisition effects separate.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 18

- Minor: The purchase prices of the two acquisitions differ between filings. Micromax is USD 500 million in the annual report, USD 493 million in the first-quarter report and release, and USD 494 million in the second- and third-quarter reports; EFC is USD 369 million in the annual report and USD 367 million in the quarterly reports. The later quarterly figures control, the earlier figures stay recorded as estimates, and nothing is averaged.

- Minor: The annual report states USD 373 million of revolver capacity net of letters of credit at 2026-02-18, which is below the USD 500 million facility less USD 7.0 million of letters of credit; the drawn balance on that date is not stated, and the first stated drawn balance is USD 85.0 million at 2026-03-31. Liquidity should use dated quarter-end figures until the February figure is explained.

- Minor: No standalone fourth-quarter 2025 results, 2025 quarterly filings or fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release were supplied. Quarterly 2025 comparatives exist only inside the 2026 filings, which state that certain prior-year amounts were reclassified. Any last-twelve-month figure needs arithmetic from the annual and nine-month figures and must say so.

- Minor: No credit rating, market quote, deal term, peer set, portfolio or prior run was supplied, as the run settings are blank for each. Ratings & triggers, Market-implied risk, Security selection and Peer benchmark cannot run, and Committee decision states the fund's limits as not supplied. The annual report mentions rating risk only in general terms.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42

- Minor: A search of all seven sources found no disclosure of restricted cash, receivables factoring, supply chain finance or securitization. Absence from the filings is not evidence of zero, so Liquidity and Financial foundation must say not disclosed rather than none.

- Minor: No Form 8-K was supplied. The merger agreement, its termination, the February 2026 credit agreement amendment and the 2026 proxy statement are known only through references in the supplied reports.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-03-31_esi-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 40; EX-99.1_2026-07-27_aearningsreleaseex99120266.htm.jsonl, page 8

- Resolved: The second-quarter report and release describe the Solstice merger as pending, with closing expected in the first half of 2027, while the third-quarter report and release state it was terminated on 2026-08-27 with a mutual release. The later documents control; the earlier description is superseded and is not used as a current fact.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_esi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-07-27_aearningsreleaseex99120266.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 4

spans.text: ## Request

Financial foundation for Element Solutions Inc (issuer id esi) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway: normalised statements, debt, leverage, cover and liquidity from the seven supplied filings and releases, consolidated group, USD millions. Source readiness (CP-0) was supplied and is relied on for the source inventory and conflicts.
## Sources

Document dates for the annual report and the quarterly reports are the signature dates printed in each report; the annual report's filing date is also stated in the third quarterly report. No supplied document is dated after 2026-11-05.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Element Solutions' debt-funded 2026 acquisitions lifted net debt to USD 1,857.2 million at 2026-09-30, 3.29x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA against 2.13x at the 2025 year-end, but interest cover of 6.59x and USD 478.0 million of undrawn revolver keep creditor protection adequate.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–18

The year-end net leverage of 2.13x becomes 3.96x pro forma for the two acquisitions closed in January and February 2026, and the 2026-09-30 ratio still overstates the burden because acquired earnings enter only from closing; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA net leverage is 2.76x. The first large maturity is the USD 800.0 million senior notes due 2028-09-01, and covenant headroom cannot be measured because the covenant EBITDA definition is not supplied.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C12; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18
### Leverage and coverage

Net debt at carrying value rose by USD 857.8 million between the 2025 year-end and 2026-09-30 because USD 865.8 million of payments for the EFC and Micromax acquisitions, closed in January and February 2026, were funded by USD 449.4 million of add-on term loan proceeds, USD 15.0 million of net revolver borrowings and a USD 401.6 million fall in cash. Net leverage on reported EBITDA moved from 2.13x (3.96x pro forma for the two acquisitions) to 3.29x and total leverage from 3.46x to 3.69x, after a fall from 2.92x in 2024.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46

The increase is overstated as a measure of risk because last-twelve-months reported EBITDA of USD 564.8 million holds the acquired earnings only from 2026-01-02 and 2026-02-02, while the debt is counted in full; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 673.1 million the same net debt is 2.76x and total debt is 3.09x. The adjusted figure is the contrary evidence, but it adds back USD 52.6 million of acquisition and integration costs in nine months 2026 and added back USD 37.1 million of executive share grants in FY2025, so it cannot be treated as free of one-offs.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 124

Interest cover is the offsetting strength: reported EBITDA covers cash interest 6.59x on a last-twelve-months basis (7.85x on adjusted EBITDA), against 6.85x in FY2025, because about 94% of debt is fixed through swaps and the senior notes due 2028 carry a fixed coupon. Cash interest rose USD 17.1 million in nine months 2026 to USD 76.2 million, so run-rate interest sits above the last-twelve-months figure until a full year of interest on the add-on term loans is paid.
Basis: calculation C07; calculation C11; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 9
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow was USD 192.2 million in nine months 2026 against USD 198.7 million a year earlier even though reported EBITDA rose from USD 389.1 million to USD 483.7 million, because receivables absorbed USD 137.3 million and inventories USD 80.7 million as pass-through metal prices rose. After capital expenditure of USD 83.4 million, operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 108.8 million, which only just covered dividends of USD 59.3 million and buybacks of USD 37.7 million, together USD 97.0 million and leaving USD 11.8 million, so the acquisitions were funded from debt and the cash balance.
Basis: calculation C09; calculation C17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–46

The working-capital drag is partly timing: third-quarter operating cash flow was USD 159.2 million after a first-quarter outflow of USD 66.6 million, and last-twelve-months operating cash flow of USD 283.3 million less capital expenditure of USD 100.4 million leaves USD 182.9 million. All of the buybacks came in the third quarter, with USD 35.0 million of revolver borrowings repaid in the same quarter, and a further rise in metal prices or a reversal of Electronics demand would extend the working-capital drag.
Basis: calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C17; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 8
### Liquidity and maturities

Cash fell to USD 224.9 million at 2026-09-30, of which USD 176 million sits in foreign subsidiaries, so liquidity rests on the USD 500.0 million revolving facility maturing in 2031, which had USD 15.0 million drawn and USD 7.0 million of letters of credit and so USD 478.0 million undrawn. No bullet maturity falls due before the USD 800.0 million senior notes on 2028-09-01, followed by USD 1,279.7 million of term loans on 2030-12-18, and no committed facility expires within twelve months; the filings print no by-year schedule at the latest date, and quarterly term loan repayments of USD 3.2 million occurred in the second and third quarters.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9

The risk is a 2028 refinancing of the senior notes at a coupon above their current fixed rate while the revolver remains the only committed source, but the springing first lien net leverage covenant of 5.0 to 1.0 applies only when revolver borrowings exceed 30% of the commitment, so it does not constrain today's USD 15.0 million draw. The reported covenant ratio and its EBITDA definition are not printed, so headroom is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18
### Definitions and data quality

Three definition differences change a reader's figures: debt at carrying value is USD 12.6 million below contractual principal, which is the gap between the issuer's own net debt of USD 1,869.8 million and the carrying-value net debt used here; the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA margin switched in 2026 to a denominator that excludes pass-through metals, so the FY2025 margin of 21.5% and the nine-month 2026 margin of 27.9% are not comparable; and purchase prices for both acquisitions differ between the annual report and the quarterly reports, where the later figures of USD 494 million and USD 367 million are used.

Basis: calculation C04; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

Standalone fourth-quarter 2025 results and 2025 quarterly filings were not supplied, so last-twelve-months figures are built from the annual and nine-month figures and carry the prior-year reclassification risk the filings state. Segment results are available only as the two reportable segments, and no corporate or elimination line is printed.
### Events after the balance sheet

The FY2025 balance sheet pre-dates the EFC acquisition of 2026-01-02 and the Micromax acquisition of 2026-02-02, so year-end net debt of USD 999.4 million understates the position the creditor now faces; adding the acquisition cash paid gives pro forma net debt of USD 1,860.4 million and 3.96x FY2025 reported EBITDA before any acquired earnings. A further USD 9.7 million Kuprion milestone payment falls in the fourth quarter of 2026, after the latest balance sheet, and the Solstice merger agreement of 2026-07-06 was terminated on 2026-08-27 with no payment stated.

## Gaps

- High: The covenant EBITDA definition and the reported first lien net leverage ratio are not printed; only a compliance statement is given. Covenant headroom is therefore not established, and no covenant conclusion should rest on the consolidated leverage ratios computed here. The executed Credit Agreement and the compliance certificate would close this.

- Medium: Last-twelve-months EBITDA to 2026-09-30 includes EFC from 2026-01-02 and Micromax from 2026-02-02 only, while debt is counted in full, so leverage at 2026-09-30 is overstated against run-rate. Pro forma acquired EBITDA for the full period is not stated; the issuer states only a nine-month figure assuming the Micromax acquisition closed on 2026-01-01 and a 2026 guidance figure.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Medium: The term loan principal is not scheduled by year at 2026-09-30, and USD 12.9 million of current installments beyond the USD 15.0 million revolver borrowings is not itemised. The maturity ladder places the term loans at 2030-12-18, so earlier amortisation is not shown. The Credit Agreement amortisation schedule would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 8

- Medium: The filings print a dash for several lines in some periods, and each dash is treated as not supplied rather than zero: current installments of long-term debt at 2025-12-31, income from discontinued operations in FY2025, acquisition spend in FY2025 and nine months 2025, debt proceeds in FY2025 and nine months 2025, share repurchases in FY2024, financing fees in FY2025 and nine months 2025, disposal and divestiture proceeds in FY2024 and nine months 2026, non-controlling interest in the third quarters, and the add-backs for the inventory step-up, the divestiture result, debt financing costs and contingent consideration in the periods where they did not arise. The lines affected are visible in the statement tables and none is needed for a ratio; confirmation from the issuer would close them.

- Low: Some statement lines exist in only one type of filing: net income from continuing operations, discontinued operations and held-for-sale lines appear in the annual statements only, and the contingent consideration line, lines of credit and the financing fee line appear in the quarterly statements only. The interim columns show those lines as not supplied.

- Low: The undrawn revolver at 2024-12-31 is not stated; the annual report gives unused capacity of USD 368 million at 2025-12-31 and combined availability of about USD 390 million across all facilities at both year-ends. The liquidity table shows the 2024 figure as not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114

- Low: Quarterly lease liabilities are not printed in the third-quarter report, so the lease obligation at 2026-09-30 is not supplied; the annual report gives USD 86.0 million at 2025-12-31 against USD 81.6 million a year earlier. Lease liabilities sit in accrued and other liabilities and are not in Total Debt.

- Low: The 10-Q prints no cash interest or tax supplement, so nine-month cash interest paid comes from the third-quarter release; a Q4 2025 stand-alone period and the 2025 quarterly filings are not supplied, so any quarterly trend before 2026 is not available.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85

- Low: The segment note gives no corporate or elimination line and no segment Adjusted EBITDA by product line, so Micromax and EFC earnings are not stated separately; maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not split; and the revolver borrowings of USD 15.0 million are presented within current installments although the facility matures in 2031.
- Low: The 10-Q states that certain prior-year amounts were reclassified but does not quantify them, so the 2025 comparative columns may differ slightly from the 2025 annual report presentation.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12

Business, ownership, transaction and governance fact pack for Element Solutions Inc (issuer id esi) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway, from the seven supplied filings and releases. Source readiness (CP-0) was supplied and is relied on for the source inventory.

Document dates are the signature dates printed in the annual report and the quarterly reports. No supplied document is dated after 2026-11-05.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Element Solutions is a widely held, acquisitive specialty-chemicals group with no controlling sponsor identified, so governance risk is medium and rests on financial policy rather than extraction: debt-funded 2026 acquisitions and buybacks are the behaviours creditors should monitor.

The business sells consumable electronics and industrial materials with no customer at 10% of net sales, but Electronics is 77.5% of nine-month 2026 net sales and the two acquisitions closed in January and February 2026 added USD 389.3 million to nine-month net sales. A merger with Solstice was agreed on 2026-07-06 and terminated on 2026-08-27 with a mutual release and no payment stated.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26
### Key findings

The operating model is a consumables franchise whose revenue visibility is short. Customers reorder products consumed in their production lines and none reaches 10% of net sales, which limits single-customer loss, but order backlog is minimal, so a fall in electronics demand reaches revenue within quarters rather than being cushioned by contracted volume. Electronics produced 76.2% of segment Adjusted EBITDA in nine months 2026, so creditors are exposed to one demand cycle, led by the AI infrastructure demand that management itself cites.

Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 16; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27

Acquisitions have changed the credit profile within one year. Micromax and EFC cost USD 861 million in cash, were funded by USD 450 million of add-on term loans plus cash and revolver borrowings, and brought USD 389.3 million of nine-month 2026 net sales, 13.8% of the total. The purchase accounting assigns USD 235.0 million and USD 172.0 million to identifiable intangibles and USD 128.9 million and USD 163.8 million to goodwill, USD 699.7 million of the USD 877.0 million total consideration, so most of the price is intangible value that depends on the acquired earnings arriving, and EFC executives hold performance units that vest on 2028 and 2030 EFC earnings, so the full cost stays open until then.
Basis: calculation C04; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 126

Sponsor and governance risk is medium on the evidence available. No controlling holder or sponsor is identified, the company is listed, and the documented behaviours are mostly ordinary: a fixed quarterly dividend, USD 200 million of term loan prepayment funded by the 2025 sale of the printing plate business, and a related-party advisory fee of USD 2.0 million a year, which is 0.37% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA and was extended on 2026-05-05 to a three-year term. The softer signal is capital return while leverage was rising: dividends and buybacks of USD 97.0 million in nine months 2026 absorbed 50.5% of operating cash flow, with all of the USD 37.7 million of buybacks in the third quarter, almost all of it in September after the merger was terminated.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47

The terminated Solstice merger shows willingness to pursue a transformative transaction. The agreement of 2026-07-06 would have made the company a wholly owned subsidiary of Solstice for half a Solstice share and USD 10.00 in cash per share, and carried a possible company termination fee of USD 376 million, which would have been paid from cash or the revolver. The termination on 2026-08-27 removed that contingency and the change of control, and no payment is stated, but the company has shown that a large combination is on its agenda, and the change-of-control terms of its notes and loans are not available to test.

Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but has three definitional soft spots. The adjusted EBITDA margin moved in 2026 to a denominator that excludes pass-through metals, prior-year amounts were reclassified without quantification, and annual-report purchase prices for both acquisitions differ from the later quarterly figures. None blocks monitoring, and each is logged in the conflict register, but together they mean year-on-year margin comparisons must be rebuilt rather than read across.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a medium risk reading is that the business is better protected than backlog and concentration suggest: products are consumed in manufacturing, the customer base is diversified, switching costs are described as high, and management reports third-quarter organic growth of 13% with record results. That supports a lower governance and business risk reading if growth proves durable and the acquisitions integrate as presented.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 16; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8

The view would move to high risk if capital returns were debt-funded while leverage stayed elevated, for instance buybacks continuing at the third-quarter pace of USD 37.7 million a quarter while revolver borrowings rise, or if a further large combination were announced before the 2026 acquisitions are absorbed. It would move to low risk if the proxy statement showed independent board control and no related-party leakage beyond the advisory fee, and if the credit agreement showed restricted-payment capacity that is tight relative to current leverage. Evidence that electronics demand is slowing, such as falling organic growth in the Electronics segment from 18% in nine months 2026, would raise business risk independently of governance.
Basis: calculation C06; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47
### Limitations

- The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so board independence, control rights, executive pay and share ownership are not established; this keeps governance risk at medium rather than low and prevents any statement that no holder controls the company.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75

- The executed credit agreement and indenture were not supplied, so restricted-payment, debt and lien capacity and the change-of-control terms are not established; financial policy is judged from behaviour only, and capacity is not separated from willingness.

- Earnings of Micromax and EFC are not stated separately beyond net sales, so the conclusion that the acquisitions add earnings to cover their financing rests on segment growth rather than on acquired EBITDA.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18

- Merger and termination terms are known only from the quarterly summaries and no stand-alone agreement was supplied, so the statement that no termination payment was made rests on the absence of a stated payment.

Scope is business quality, financial profile, downside path and monitoring triggers, with no security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Element Solutions has an adequate fundamental credit profile: consumable-driven, diversified earnings and 6.59x interest cover support debt service, but debt-funded 2026 acquisitions lifted net leverage to 3.29x, so creditors rely on acquired earnings arriving before the USD 800.0 million notes mature in 2028.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05

Net leverage was 2.13x at the 2025 year-end and is 3.96x pro forma for the two acquisitions closed on 2026-01-02 and 2026-02-02, before any acquired earnings; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA it is 2.76x at 2026-09-30. Cash plus undrawn revolver of USD 702.9 million covers 0.88x of the 2028 notes, and covenant headroom cannot be measured.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05; calculation C08
### Key findings

Revenue is durable but tied to one cycle. Customers reorder products consumed in their production lines and no customer reaches 10% of net sales, but Electronics is 77.5% of nine-month 2026 net sales and 76.2% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, order backlog is minimal and organic growth of 13% leans on AI infrastructure demand, so a demand slowdown would reach earnings within quarters.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 8

Margin resilience is better than reported margins suggest. Gross margin fell to 35.51% in nine months 2026 from 42.34%, and Adjusted EBITDA over total net sales fell by 2.86 percentage points to 19.08%, but pass-through metals of 31.7% of net sales add sales at little margin, and the issuer's margin excluding them rose by 110 bp to 27.9%. Creditors should therefore track EBITDA dollars and the ex-metals margin, not margin on total sales.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62

Cash conversion weakened in 2026 and is the main watch point. Working capital absorbed USD 174.1 million in nine months 2026 against USD 78.4 million a year earlier as metal prices rose, so operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 108.8 million against USD 153.5 million, and dividends and buybacks of USD 97.0 million took most of it. The last-twelve-months figure of USD 182.9 million shows the drag is partly timing.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45

Leverage is the weakest dimension. Net debt of USD 1,857.2 million is 3.29x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, or 2.76x issuer-adjusted EBITDA, because debt was drawn in full for acquisitions whose earnings enter from closing; the reported ratio therefore overstates run-rate leverage, while the adjusted ratio depends on add-backs that include USD 52.6 million of integration and transaction costs in nine months 2026. A USD 100.0 million shortfall in last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA would lift net leverage on that measure from 2.76x to 3.24x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C07

Liquidity is adequate and the maturity wall is distant but not covered. Cash of USD 224.9 million and USD 478.0 million of undrawn revolver total USD 702.9 million against USD 800.0 million of notes due 2028-09-01, a USD 97.1 million shortfall that cash generation or a refinancing must close. The springing first lien test applies only if revolver borrowings exceed USD 150.0 million, USD 135.0 million above today's draw, and the reported covenant ratio is not printed.
Basis: calculation C05; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Interest rate risk returns before the 2030 maturities. About 94% of debt is fixed through swaps, which hold the effective term loan rate near 4.4%, but swaps covering USD 690 million expire in December 2028 and USD 483 million in December 2029, and refinancing the 2028 notes at a higher coupon adds USD 8.0 million of annual interest for each 100 bp, 9.3% of last-twelve-months cash interest.
Basis: calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 9

Financial policy risk is medium. No controlling sponsor is identified and the dividend is modest, but acquisitions and buybacks proceeded while leverage rose, and the merger with Solstice was agreed and terminated within weeks, which shows appetite for transformative deals.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest argument for a stronger profile is that leverage is lower than it looks. Issuer-adjusted net leverage is 2.76x, interest cover is 6.59x, 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to about USD 720 million including full-year contributions from both acquisitions, and last-twelve-months operating cash flow less capital expenditure of USD 182.9 million compares with USD 227.6 million in FY2025, so the 2026 drag is partly timing. If fourth-quarter results confirm the guidance and working capital reverses as metal prices stabilise, net leverage on a full-year earnings base would fall without any debt repayment.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C04; calculation C07; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The view would weaken if Electronics organic growth slows from 18% toward zero, if operating cash flow stays below dividends plus buybacks, if revolver borrowings rise above the springing threshold, or if a further large transaction is announced before the 2026 acquisitions are absorbed. It would strengthen if the notes due 2028 are refinanced early at a modest coupon increase, or if executed loan documents show tight restricted-payment capacity and a covenant ratio with wide headroom.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C05; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Limitations

- No agency rating, market quote or peer set was supplied, so the adequate label is an analyst judgement against general leveraged-credit norms rather than against named peers or market pricing; relative standing and refinancing pricing are not established.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- Forward earnings are known only through one-year management guidance and no lender projections, so the conclusion that leverage falls as acquired earnings arrive rests on guidance rather than a model.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-07-27_aearningsreleaseex99120266.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Metal price sensitivity, customer-level concentration and end-market percentages are not disclosed, so the conclusion that margin and cash conversion recover as metal prices stabilise is directional only.
- The covenant EBITDA definition and reported ratio are not printed, so the liquidity conclusion treats the springing test as dormant on the basis of the current draw only.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18

### Company description

Element Solutions formulates specialty chemistries and materials that customers consume in manufacturing, in two segments: Electronics, which supplies assembly materials, circuit-board and semiconductor chemistries and, since 2026-02-02, advanced inks and pastes, and Specialties, which supplies industrial surface finishing and offshore energy fluids and, since 2026-01-02, high-purity specialty gases. Because products are consumed in production and replaced as customers produce, revenue recurs without contracted backlog, and the electronics share of net sales has risen to 77.5% with the acquisitions; this supports cash-flow visibility in normal demand but ties debt service to electronics hardware output and to the integration of two acquired businesses.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8, 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26
### Ownership and group structure

The company is a listed Delaware corporation with no controlling sponsor identified, so extraction by an owner is not a documented risk; the group borrows through the parent and its co-borrower MacDermid, Incorporated, guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries on a first-lien secured basis, while the 2028 notes carry senior unsecured guarantees from generally the same subsidiaries. The related-party advisory fee of USD 2.0 million a year is small, and the sponsor and governance risk level from Business & governance is medium because capital returns and acquisitions continued as leverage rose and the proxy statement and executed loan documents were not supplied.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 18, 26
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Volume growth is led by AI infrastructure and other high-performance electronics, with Electronics organic growth of 18% against 2% for Specialties in nine months 2026, while reported growth of 50% is lifted by acquisitions and by pass-through metals pricing of USD 891.6 million of net sales. Pricing power is shown by the issuer's margin excluding metals rising rather than falling, switching costs from customer qualification, and no customer at 10% of net sales; the exposure is that metal price moves change reported sales and working capital without changing underlying demand, and that minimal backlog gives no contractual cushion.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 16; calculation C03
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Selling, technical, general and administrative expense fell to 21.24% of net sales in nine months 2026 from 25.13%, partly because metals inflate the denominator, and capital expenditure of USD 62.2 million in FY2025 shows a modest fixed-asset base because the company blends purchased raw materials rather than manufacturing basic chemicals. Acquisition, integration and transaction costs of USD 52.6 million were added back to Adjusted EBITDA in nine months 2026, so margin defence depends on integration costs ending; specialties margin fell in the third quarter on higher corporate cost allocation, which is the segment to watch.
Basis: calculation C02; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital expenditure was 2.44% of FY2025 net sales and is expected at about USD 110 million for 2026 for Kuprion capacity and plant consolidation, so free cash flow of USD 227.6 million in FY2025 was 41.56% of Adjusted EBITDA and covered the dividend of USD 77.8 million 2.93 times. In 2026 working capital, higher cash interest and integration costs reduced conversion, and capital expenditure can be deferred as the main flexible lever, with dividends and buybacks the next.
Basis: calculation C04; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44
### Porter's Five Forces

Rivalry is moderate: named competitors include larger groups, but competition is on qualification, technology and service, which favours incumbents with embedded products. New entrants face qualification and technical-service barriers, which protects margin; substitutes arise through technology change such as chromium-free plating, which the company addresses with research and development. Buyer power is limited by diversification, as no customer reaches 10% of net sales, but large electronics manufacturers can resist price outside qualified products; supplier power is low for most raw materials, which are obtainable from multiple sources, with metals priced through to customers.
### PEST analysis

Regulatory and trade factors are material: tariffs and trade policy can change cost and demand, and about 79% of FY2025 net sales came from outside the United States, so currency translation and geopolitical disruption affect reported results; the economic driver that matters most is metal prices, which move sales and working capital. Interest-rate exposure is largely hedged until the swaps expire in December 2028 and December 2029, and the technological driver is AI-related electronics demand, which sets the growth rate of the largest segment.
### SWOT

Strengths are consumable recurring demand, no customer at 10% of net sales, interest cover of 6.59x and USD 702.9 million of liquidity; weaknesses are electronics concentration, higher leverage after the acquisitions, working-capital absorption and covenant opacity. Opportunities that would improve credit quality are acquired earnings arriving ahead of guidance and early refinancing of the 2028 notes; threats are an electronics demand slowdown, a metal price reversal that strains working capital, and a further large transaction before integration is complete.
Basis: calculation C05; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to 24 months management guides 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to about USD 720 million, raised from USD 690 million to USD 710 million in July, including a full year of both acquisitions; tailwinds are AI-driven electronics demand and acquired earnings, and headwinds are metal price volatility, tariffs, currency and integration costs. Over three to five years the debt maturities of 2028, 2030 and 2031 fall inside the horizon, so deleveraging and refinancing access matter more than growth; the guidance is a management figure, not a forecast, and no lender projection was supplied.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-07-27_aearningsreleaseex99120266.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18
### Downside scenario

A slowdown in AI-linked electronics demand would reach revenue within quarters because backlog is minimal, and Electronics produces 76.2% of segment Adjusted EBITDA; operating leverage on a cost base that includes research, technical service and integration cost would compress margin, while a fall in metal prices would release working capital and cushion cash flow. Free cash flow would fall toward the distributions it funds, and a USD 100.0 million fall in last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA would lift net leverage on that measure to 3.24x, while headroom to the springing first lien test of 5.0 to 1.0 cannot be measured because its definition is not printed. Management levers are deferring capital expenditure of about USD 110 million, suspending buybacks and using the revolver, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2028, but the notes then fall due against liquidity of USD 702.9 million.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C07; 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 44; 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16
### Overall credit view

Overall, Element Solutions presents an adequate business profile supported by consumable recurring demand, customer diversification and strong interest cover, but credit quality is constrained by higher leverage after debt-funded acquisitions and concentration in Electronics. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to modest capital intensity and a fixed-rate cost of debt, with 2026 working-capital drag expected to be partly timing. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of acquired earnings, early action on the 2028 notes and the rate environment when swaps expire. The primary downside path is an electronics demand slowdown while leverage is elevated and capital returns continue. Further analysis would require covenant definitions, ratings and market pricing, and acquired earnings. Fundamental credit assessment completed. Top risk: leverage after debt-funded acquisitions.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05; calculation C08
### Strengths and weaknesses

The principal strengths are recurring consumable demand across a diversified customer base, interest cover of 6.59x supported by fixed-rate funding, liquidity of USD 702.9 million with no bullet maturity before 2028, and a record of prepaying debt from disposal proceeds. The principal weaknesses are leverage after debt-funded acquisitions, concentration in Electronics with minimal backlog, working capital absorbing cash in 2026, and USD 800.0 million of notes due in 2028 against present liquidity.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C05

## Gaps

- High: The covenant EBITDA definition and the reported first lien net leverage ratio are not printed, so covenant headroom and the practical effect of the springing test on the revolver are not established. The executed credit agreement and compliance certificate would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18

- Medium: No agency rating, market price or peer set was supplied, so market access, refinancing pricing and standing against peers are not established; the adequate label is judged against general leveraged-credit norms. Ratings and quotes would close this.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42

- Medium: Acquired earnings of Micromax and EFC for a full period are not stated, so last-twelve-months leverage at 2026-09-30 cannot be put on a full-period basis and the 2026 guidance cannot be tested against a build-up.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Low: Metal price sensitivity of sales, working capital and margin, customer-level concentration and end-market percentages are not disclosed, so the size of any reversal in working capital is not established.
- Low: The proxy statement was not supplied, so board independence and ownership are not established for the financial policy assessment.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_esi-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 75

- Low: No schedule of term loan amortisation by year at 2026-09-30 was supplied; quarterly repayments of USD 3.2 million occurred in the second and third quarters of 2026, so the maturity profile before 2030 is approximate.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_esi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; EX-99.1_2026-10-21_aearningsreleaseex99120269.htm.jsonl, page 8
